To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CK contractions of quantum group SOq(N), which is deformed by the deformation parameter q, can be obtained by the contraction procedure, which includes analytical continuation, and the deformation parameter is transformed as follows: q --> 1/(1 + 2/q).
all CK contractions are realized for quantum orthogonal groups in Cartesian basis and the algorithm for their obtaining has been suggested.
we have found all contractions of quantum group SOq(N).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (i) to obtain all CK contractions for SOq(N), (ii) to find a general algorithm to construct all possible contractions for quantum groups, (iii) to obtain all nonequivalent (in Hopf-algebraic sense) CK contractions of quantum groups.

the following questions: What are all possible CK contractions of quantum group SOq(N)? What is the relation between these CK contractions and CK contractions of classical group SO(N)? How to describe CK contractions of a quantum group in a simple form?

the following questions: (1) What is the most general deformation of the orthogonal group? (2) What are all possible contractions and analytical continuation of the orthogonal group SO(N)? (3) How to obtain all possible contracations of SOq(N)? (4) How to realize the contracations in the Cartesian basis?

quantum orthogonal groups are as rich as their undeformed counterparts.
all CK groups are realized as contractions of quantum groups in Cartesian basis.
quantum deformation of orthogonal groups in Cartesian basis is not a unique one and it has a lot of possible contractions.

all known CK contraction of orthogonal group can be obtained by quantum deformation and contractions of quantum deformation of orthogonal groups.
